hint_annualRateExisting.message: It's on your statement or your lender's amortization schedule.

hint_rateType_nominal.message: The one each month’s interest is worked out from.

hint_rateType_effective.message: What the loan costs in a year; banks usually publish this one.

hint_method_german.message: A higher first payment that falls every month.

hint_dayCount_thirty360.message: Every month charges 30 days, even with 31 or 28.

hint_dayCount_actual360.message: Each payment charges the calendar days since the one before.

glossaryDefinition_principal.message: The money you borrow, which you pay back little by little with each payment.

glossaryExample_principal.message: Example: if you borrow $$10,000, the principal is $$10,000; interest is charged on top.

glossaryDefinition_interest.message: What you pay the lender for using its money. It is charged every month on what you still owe.

glossaryExample_interest.message: Example: on $$10,000 at 15.6 % nominal, the first month’s interest is $$130.

glossaryDefinition_term.message: How long you have to pay the loan back, in months: one payment a month.

glossaryExample_term.message: Example: a 36-month term is 3 years of payments.

glossaryDefinition_installment.message: What you pay each month. It covers part of the principal, the interest and, if any, insurance and other charges.

glossaryExample_installment.message: Example: $$10,000 over 12 months at 15.6 % nominal, French system: $$905.42 a month.

glossaryDefinition_balance.message: The principal you still owe. It goes down with every payment.

glossaryExample_balance.message: Example: in the loan above, the first payment repays $$775.42 of principal, so the balance drops to $$9,224.58.

glossaryDefinition_schedule.message: The list of all your payments: the date of each, how much goes to principal, interest and charges, and the balance left.

glossaryExample_schedule.message: Example: a 12-month loan has 12 rows, one per payment. The simulator shows it under the summary.

glossaryDefinition_amortization.message: How each payment splits between principal and interest. French: the same payment every month. German: the same principal every month, so the payment starts higher and falls.

glossaryExample_amortization.message: Example: $$10,000 over 12 months at 15.6 %: French, $$905.42 every month and $$865 of interest; German, from $$963.33 down to $$844.20 and $$845 of interest.

glossaryDefinition_nominalRate.message: The yearly rate each month’s interest is worked out from: each month charges about a twelfth of it.

glossaryDefinition_effectiveRate.message: What the loan costs in a whole year once each month’s interest also earns interest. It is a little higher than the nominal rate, and it is the one banks usually publish.

glossaryDefinition_maxRate.message: The highest effective rate a lender may charge for each kind of loan (consumer, mortgage, microcredit…), published by the Central Bank of Ecuador (BCE). It changes every few months.

glossaryExample_maxRate.message: Example: enter it and the simulator warns you when your loan’s effective rate is above it.

glossaryDefinition_dayCount.message: How many days of interest each payment charges. 30/360: every month counts 30 days. Actual days/360: each payment charges the calendar days since the one before.

glossaryExample_dayCount.message: Example: with actual days, a 31-day month charges more interest than February.

glossaryDefinition_creditLifeInsurance.message: Insurance that pays off what you still owe if you die (and, in some policies, if you become permanently disabled). It is charged every month.

glossaryExample_creditLifeInsurance.message: Example: at 0.05 % a month on a $$10,000 balance, that month’s insurance is $$5.

glossaryDefinition_solca.message: A 0.5 % contribution on loans in Ecuador that funds SOLCA, the cancer society’s hospitals. It is taken once from the amount when the loan is paid out.

glossaryExample_solca.message: Example: on a $$10,000 loan, $$50 goes to SOLCA and you receive $$9,950.

glossaryDefinition_otherCharges.message: Fixed amounts some lenders add to every payment, such as fees or extra insurance.

glossaryExample_otherCharges.message: Example: a $$2 charge on each of 12 payments adds $$24.

glossaryDefinition_totalCost.message: What you pay on top of the principal: interest, insurance, other charges and SOLCA.

glossaryExample_totalCost.message: Example: $$10,000 over 12 months at 15.6 % with SOLCA: $$865 of interest plus $$50 of SOLCA, $$915 in total.

glossaryDefinition_disbursement.message: The day the lender pays the loan out to you. With actual days, the first payment charges interest from that day.

glossaryExample_disbursement.message: Example: paid out on 10 January with the first payment on 15 February, the first payment charges 36 days of interest.

glossaryDefinition_dueDate.message: The last day to pay each payment. The payments fall on the same day of every month.

glossaryExample_dueDate.message: Example: if the first payment is due on 15 January, the next ones are due on the 15th of each month.

glossaryDefinition_extraPayment.message: Money you pay on top of your payments to lower what you owe. It first pays the interest accrued since your last due date; the rest lowers the balance.

glossaryExample_extraPayment.message: Example: after an extra payment you either keep your payment and finish sooner (reduce term), or finish on the same date with a smaller payment (reduce payment).
